transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I know the flights are short and safe, but I have this intense, over-the-top fear of getting on a plane that’s now holding me back at work. I'm hoping to get some help with it because it's really starting to limit my career.
Do you have this same intense fear or anxiety in other situations too, like elevators, bridges, crowded places, or is it mainly only when you have to fly?

No, it’s really just flying that does this to me. I have absolutely no problem with elevators, bridges, or crowded places. It's only when I have to get on an airplane that I experience this kind of intense fear.
When you have to fly or even think about flying, do you get panic-like symptoms such as a racing heart, shortness of breath, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you might lose control?

Yes, absolutely. Even just seeing a picture of a plane makes my chest tighten, my heart pound, and my palms get really sweaty. The one time I actually tried to go to the airport, I completely froze up at the gate, shaking and breathing so fast that I had to leave.
How long have you had this fear of flying, and has it been present for at least 6 months?

Yes, it has been a constant issue for about two years now, ever since my company started requiring those manager flights. I had some mild uneasiness about flying before that, but it has been a severe, unavoidable problem for the last two years, which is way past the six-month mark.
Do you also fear other specific situations or objects, or is the fear limited only to flying and airplane-related things?

No, my fear is strictly limited to flying and airplanes. I don't have any other intense fears of things like heights, animals, or other situations. This anxiety is completely and entirely focused on the prospect of being on a plane.
